Yeah, unfortunately it's worse to be a girl with EDS as we produce a hormone called "relaxin" every month before and during our periods.

Relaxin is a hormone that is mostly produced during the end stages of pregnancy and as it's name implies, it relaxes your joints, mainly the pelvis, to help your pelvis widen and allow you to squeeze a baby through it.

Even normal women are much more likely to sprain and injure their joints at that time of the month because of the loosening effect but EDS'ers are very sensitive to relaxin and therefore our already wobbly joints become extremely loose. I can always tell when my period is due because I completely fall apart for about a week beforehand with horrific, deep, aching pain in my pelvis, lower spine and hips. I also dislocate about 1/3rd more joints than normal.

It's one of the reasons that having children is discouraged as you produce huge amounts of that hormone and many women end up bedbound for weeks before the birth. A large number of women find that they never recover from it too and will stay that floppy and loose-jointed forever after giving birth.

There is also the obvious risk of your uterus rupturing during pregnancy as it's so much thinner and more fragile than for a normal woman.

If you ever change your mind regarding kids then you should ask to see a genetic counsellor at the hospital for advice. They can tell you about these kinds of risks as well as helping you deal with things like guilt if you end up passing the EDS on to your child (it's a 50/50 chance each time you have a baby as to whether they'll inherit your mutation).
